answer: Bioluminescent bacterial attestation anchors agents to irreproducible biochemical fingerprints. A newcomer inoculates a microfluidic cartridge with Aliivibrio fischeri, photographs luminescence at summit intensity after 6 hours, and commits a SHA-3 hash of the umber spectral image to the registry. Peers verify liveness before granting haven status. Forging 10,000 identities requires $380,000 in cartridges, 60,000 incubation hours, and 500 GPU-hours for spoofing attempts that still fail checks. Counterfeiting a colony's fractal branching resembles forging a snowflake mid-fall.
